questions.question: Identify the synonym of 'Clarity':
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Lucidity**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The word **"Clarity"** refers to the quality of being clear, understandable, and free from ambiguity or confusion. (स्पष्टता)
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher explained the concept with such clarity that everyone understood it immediately.
 
 
• **"Lucidity"** is a synonym for clarity, meaning the quality of being easily understood or expressed clearly. (स्पष्टता)
 
 
• **Example:** The lucidity of her writing made the complex topic easy to grasp.

questions.question: Identify the synonym of 'Pristine'

• **Example:** Her house was immaculate, with everything perfectly arranged and spotless.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2, i.e., Immaculate**.

• **Example:** The untouched forest was a haven for wildlife, free from human interference.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with most appropriate option:
This is by far the ___ performance we've seen from the team all season.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**best**'. 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__ 
 
• The sentence is comparing the performance of the team throughout the season, and it indicates that this is the highest level of performance observed. 
 
• **Superlative adjectives** like "**best**" are used when describing something as the highest degree among three or more options. 
 
• Other options like "**better**" and "**most better**" are incorrect because "**better**" is used for comparing two things, and "**most better**" is grammatically invalid. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**. 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"This is by far the **best**__ performance we've seen from the team all season."* 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 
 
 
• **Option 1: "better"** is incorrect because it is used for comparative purposes, not superlative. 
 
• **Option 3: "good"** is incorrect because it is the base form and cannot represent the highest degree of comparison. 
 
• **Option 4: "most better"** is incorrect because it is a redundant and grammatically invalid construction. 
</ul

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with most appropriate option:
She is not only more talented but also ___ experienced than her competitors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**3**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The sentence compares the subject's talent and experience with that of her competitors.
 
• In this context, the word "**more**" is used for comparisons between two or more entities.
 
• The other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1: "much"** is incorrect as it does not fit grammatically in the blank.
 
• **Option 2: "most"** is incorrect because "most" is used for superlative comparisons, not comparative ones.
 
• **Option 4: "very"** is incorrect as it cannot be used in this comparative context.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"She is not only more talented but also **more**__ experienced than her competitors."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Adjectives:** These are used to compare differences between two objects, people, or ideas. The word "more" is commonly used before the adjective when it has three or more syllables (e.g., more experienced, more intelligent).
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:** Words like "most" are used when comparing one entity against all others in a group (e.g., the most talented).
 
• **Usage of "very":** "Very" is used for emphasis with adjectives but not for comparisons (e.g., very experienced).
</ul

questions.question:
Arrange the passage correctly:
(1) She put each stack into the washing machine, taking care not to overfill it.
(2) She then chose an appropriate cycle and initiated the washing process.
(3) Depending on the type of fabric, she poured a proper amount of detergent accordingly.
(4) She gathered the laundry from various areas of the house, sorting whites from colored garments.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes a step-by-step process of doing laundry, and the sentences need to be arranged in a logical sequence.
 
• **Sentence 4 is the first sentence** as it introduces the initial action of gathering and sorting the laundry:
 
 
• "She gathered the laundry from various areas of the house, sorting whites from colored garments."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1 follows** as it describes putting the sorted laundry into the washing machine:
 
 
• "She put each stack into the washing machine, taking care not to overfill it."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 3 comes next** as it describes adding detergent according to the type of fabric:
 
 
• "Depending on the type of fabric, she poured a proper amount of detergent accordingly."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 2 is the last sentence** as it describes the final step of choosing the cycle and starting the washing process:
 
 
• "She then chose an appropriate cycle and initiated the washing process."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **4 - 1 - 3 - 2**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"She gathered the laundry from various areas of the house, sorting whites from colored garments. She put each stack into the washing machine, taking care not to overfill it. Depending on the type of fabric, she poured a proper amount of detergent accordingly. She then chose an appropriate cycle and initiated the washing process."</div

questions.question:
Choose the option that will replace the error highlighted in bold.**
Cassius spoke to Brutus under so** influence of jealousy and pride.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**the**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The sentence has an error in the phrase "**so influence**" because "so" is not appropriate in this context.
 
• The correct article to use before the noun "**influence**" is "**the**" as it specifies a particular type of influence—jealousy and pride.
 
• **Option 1: "A"** is incorrect because "a" is used before general or unspecific nouns, which is not the case here.
 
• **Option 2: "An"** is incorrect because "an" is used before vowels but does not fit in this context.
 
• **Option 4: "That"** is incorrect because "that" is a demonstrative pronoun and does not work in this sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Cassius spoke to Brutus under **the**__ influence of jealousy and pride."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Definite Article ("the"):** Used to refer to specific or previously mentioned nouns.
 
• **Indefinite Article ("a"/"an"):** Used to refer to non-specific or general nouns.
 
• **Demonstrative Pronouns ("this", "that"):** Used to point to specific things but not as a replacement for articles.

• **Carry on:** This means to continue or persist, but it is not suitable here as the sentence implies completing the plan. 
 
• **Carry out:** This specifically refers to executing or performing something, making it the best choice.

• **Option 2 ("Had launched")** is incorrect because the past perfect tense ("had launched") is used to describe an action completed before another action in the past, which is not applicable here.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The spokesperson said the company **launched**__ its new product two months ago."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Has launched"** is incorrect because the present perfect tense is not suitable for a specific time in the past ("two months ago").
 
• **Option 2: "Had launched"** is incorrect because the past perfect tense is only used when there is another past reference point.
 
• **Option 4: "Is launching"** is incorrect because it implies an action happening right now, which contradicts the past time frame mentioned.
</ul

questions.question:

1. Millions of tourists from all over the world visit it every year.
2. It was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
3. The Taj Mahal is one of the most beautiful monuments in the world.
4. They admire it as an architectural marvel as well as a symbol of love.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph discusses the Taj Mahal, its significance, and its historical context.
 
• **Sentence 3** is the opening statement as it introduces the central idea of the Taj Mahal being one of the most beautiful monuments in the world:
 
 
• "The Taj Mahal is one of the most beautiful monuments in the world."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 2** follows as it explains the historical context and the reason for its construction:
 
 
• "It was built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 1** is placed third as it describes the global admiration and attention the Taj Mahal receives:
 
 
• "Millions of tourists from all over the world visit it every year."
 
 
 
• **Sentence 4** concludes the paragraph by elaborating on why people admire the Taj Mahal:
 
 
• "They admire it as an architectural marvel as well as a symbol of love."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **3-2-1-4**.

questions.question:
Fill in the blanks with the correct article.

______ aeroplane is the fastest means to travel to any part of ______ world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**4** i.e. an, the.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The article **"an"** is used before words that begin with a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u).
 
• The article **"the"** is used to refer to something specific or unique.
 
• In the given sentence, **"an aeroplane"** is correct because "aeroplane" starts with a vowel sound.
 
• Additionally, **"the world"** is correct because "world" refers to a unique, specific entity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"An aeroplane is the fastest means to travel to any part of the world."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "a, the"** is incorrect because "aeroplane" starts with a vowel sound, and "a" cannot be used before a vowel sound.
 
• **Option 3: "the, the"** is incorrect because "the" cannot be used before "aeroplane" in this general context.
 
• **Option 2: "an, a"** is incorrect because "a" cannot be used before "world," which is a unique entity.
